body:
Population figures this card is waiting on, re-derived locally (from #16095)

This is a measurement hand-off only. Nothing about what `os build` accepts is changed by the linked work, and the two cards are deliberately not merged.

#16095 needed the same population number and could not reuse the figure in its own description: the widely quoted "39 of 39 hooks are handler-authored, 24 of 31 actions are body-authored" was measured against the reference CRM's pinned `@objectstack/lint@17.3.0`, which is outside the platform repository and is **not** reproducible in this tree.

Re-derived against this repository's own four example apps (`examples/app-crm`, `app-showcase`, `app-todo`, `app-multi-package`), loading each real config through `loadConfig` and `normalizeStackInput`:

| app | hooks | handler-authored | body-authored | actions | action body-authored |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| app-crm | 1 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| app-showcase | 4 | 0 | 4 | 139 | 125 |
| app-todo | 1 | 1 | 0 | 16 | 0 |
| app-multi-package | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **total** | **6** | **2** | **4** | **157** | **125** |

Two readings worth carrying into this card:

- **Hook authorship in this tree is mixed, not dominated by either shape** — 2 of 6 handler-authored. The reference app's ratio is much stronger, so a decision calibrated only on this repository's examples will understate the handler population that real apps carry, and one calibrated only on the reference app cannot be checked in CI here.
- **Actions are overwhelmingly body-authored** — 125 of 157 — which is consistent with the standing finding that the action-body door reaches its intake and is not a defect.

Every inline handler in the table lowers cleanly: `lowerCallables` produced a `body.language === 'js'` for all 6 hooks, so none of them is in the refused-extraction class.

Method note, since the number is the point here: the counts come from the normalized stack rather than from source-text grepping, so a hook registered through a package manifest or an object's `actions` array is counted the same way the compiler counts it.

## H9 repaired — this hold's trigger existed for readers and not for the machine, for 11 days

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), body edited 2026-09-11T13:00:00Z (API `updated_at`). ⛔ No label moved: this card stays `pm:on-hold`, and ⛔ no condition was invented, widened or narrowed.

### What was wrong

This card was filed by this same seat on 2026-08-31 with a section headed `## Restart-when — a predicate, not a reminder`, and the section is good — it names the instrument, the code path and the numeric threshold. **But a heading is prose.** The hold-hygiene check and the unlock scan both read a line whose key is followed immediately by a colon and a value, anchored at the start of the line; this card had the key followed by an em dash, inside a `##` heading. Measured with the patrol's own reader before the edit: **0 values in the body, 0 in the comment channel**, against a firing positive control.

⇒ For 11 days this was a `pm:on-hold` card with **no machine-fireable exit** — the shape the state model forbids outright («两种拼写之外的 hold ⛔ 不合法»).

### What the edit added

The section's own predicate, on one readable line directly beneath its heading:

```
Restart-when: re-run #13651's census on the real build path (`loadConfig` → `normalizeStackInput` → `lowerCallables`, classified off the reason strings `extractHookBody` actually produces, ⛔ nothing re-implemented) and fire when `silent_downgrade_warnings > 0` in any measured tree.
```

Read back through the same reader: **1 value.** Labels unchanged (`domain:cli, pm:on-hold, priority:p3`).

⛔ **No trigger-file line was added, deliberately.** The sibling repair on #13776 gained two, because that card's predicate is literally a file-content predicate. This card's predicate is a **measured population number**, not a file edit: touching `packages/cli/src/hook-body.ts` does not make `silent_downgrade_warnings` rise, and nominating it would fence every future dispatch on that file behind a hold it cannot discharge. ⇒ the one required line, and nothing beyond what this card already ruled.

⚠️ And the card's own warning survives the repair intact and is worth restating, because the readable line could otherwise be misread as easier to fire than it is: it does **not** wake on "the rule shipped" — shipping is not reporting, and the number is the trigger. The measured zero in #13651 was **avoidance, not absence** (the reference app reads zero because all 39 callables were already written defensively, behind eight bespoke pins), and a zero inside this tree says nothing about apps outside it on a published CLI.

### Why this is worth a comment rather than a silent fix

This is the **fourth** instance of one defect class disposed in this lane today, across three different directives: a decorated key (#17680), a key written mid-line (#16613), a condition left in prose with no key at all (#15638), and now a key followed by an em dash instead of a colon. ⇒ **A state whose only exit is machine-gated is only as real as the line the machine reads**, and every one of these was written by a seat that believed it had recorded the condition.
